# S35 — Runs skipped at recovery or failed in the background stay visible

From the S17 review, not fixed. A run skipped at daemon recovery stays non-final, and a failed background engine job is invisible to the owner (nothing records the failure on the run).

**Findings:**  · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**2026-10-20** — Proposed, awaiting owner: a run that failed to reconcile does not count as active, so it does not block idle exit; it still shows and keeps stop and retry.

trust: unverified; by: Jon R

## Failing tests

- Per decision 116 (no new final state), a run whose Reconcile fails at recovery stays in the run manager. A stop on it answers with the run, not "no run" (TestRecoverySkipsBadRuns, kill case, rewritten).
- The skipped run's error shows on its wire row (EngineRun.Error) and in ork status and the Overview row. Its state is unchanged.
- A background job that returns an error keeps the error on the wire row in daemon memory; the state stays as the engine left it (new TestBackgroundErrorStaysOnTheWireRow).
- run.json has no error key after a failed background job (read the file back).
- The next job (retry, stop or approve) clears the error. A stop that cancels a busy job does not record context.Canceled as a failure.
- Healthy recovered runs and healthy background jobs are unchanged (existing TestRecoveredRunCanBeStoppedAndActiveRunIsPaused).

- Folded in from the S05 review (2026-10-20): recovery also skips a non-final run, queued or not, whose project is no longer registered (recoverRuns, "project ... is not registered"). The run is not in the run manager, so it cannot be stopped, yet activeRunsLocked counts it from the store and it holds the daemon up forever. Proposed test: such a run shows in the status with an error naming the missing project, does not block idle exit, and a stop answers (see Implement, Open).

A run that failed to reconcile and is kept in the manager does not count as active: it does not block idle exit or daemon stop without --force (runs.go:166-176, :184). It still shows with its error, and stop and retry still work. Test: a daemon holding only a failed-to-reconcile run exits idle.

Line numbers above into internal/daemon/runs.go predate S05 (landed 67521b0, which moved recoverRuns to :118-157 and launchRun to :389-417); find them again before editing. S05 also keeps a recovered queued run in the manager without Reconcile.
Folded in from the S05 review: the unregistered-project skip in recoverRuns (:136-139) follows the same keep-and-show rule as a failed Reconcile. Open: engine.Load needs a registry.Project (engine.Load(d.runDeps(p), p, r)), and there is none for a removed project, so how a stop works for such a run is not decided. Candidates: stop it from the stored record alone, or leave it visible with the error and no actions. S38 (projects rm refuses while the project has unfinished runs) makes this state rare. The owner decides.

Re-anchor and owner decisions of 2026-10-24 (from the S35 preflight). Anchors in internal/daemon/runs.go: recoverRuns :118-157 (unregistered-project skip :136-139, Reconcile skip :147-150), launchRun ~:611-640 (result.err set in the goroutine), activeRunsLocked ~:178-200, engineRuns ~:790-840; spec steps 2-6 are otherwise implementable as written. S77 added StopQueued("project was removed") in startQueuedLocked but only for queued runs already in the manager; recoverRuns still drops a queued run of an unregistered project before it gets there. Decisions: (1) UNREGISTERED PROJECT at recovery: a queued run is stopped from the stored record with the reason "project was removed" (as S77); a non-queued (running) run is kept visible in Needs you with an error naming the missing project and no actions (engine.Load needs a registry.Project that no longer exists). (2) IDLE EXIT: a run that failed to reconcile does not count as active, tracked by a separate flag in managedRun (not the shared failure error); a run that failed in the background (non-final state, error on the wire row, adj 116) still counts as active. The spec test "a daemon holding only a failed-to-reconcile run exits idle" holds. (3) STOP on a kept failed-to-reconcile run: stop runs Reconcile first; when it fails again the reply is the error with the run record attached (not "no run"), and the run stays non-final with the new error recorded; a final state is never reconciled again (adj 116), so a run is never finalised without a successful Reconcile. Nothing is open.

Owner decisions of 2026-10-24 on the three points the implementer raised after the first answers: (1) The stop reply keeps (record, error) at the Go ownerRun level; the wire handler still returns only the error, and the wire row shows the unchanged state and the new Error after a failed stop. No ipc.Error data field. (2) A kept run whose project is no longer registered appears as a pseudo-project group named from the recorded project name, flagged unavailable, in the status call and the TUI (reuse the project-row plumbing; no new screen); this is a wire and UI shape change in source and the TUI, so the UI pass (r14) reviews it; add the Files it touches (internal/daemon status and snapshot code, internal/source/source.go, internal/tui sidebar and overview, internal/cli status) and mark the fields *proposed* in the docs. (3) Add an optional `EngineRun.unavailable` bool (omitempty, *proposed*) set on the no-engine row; the TUI hides retry, stop, approve and answer on it. Nothing is open.
